notes: Sedgemire's causeways, boardwalks and tracks (docs/WORLD_LIFE_ROADS.md). The marsh has no road-robbers of the Vale's kind: the drowned, the leech-hounds, the sallowjaws and the wisps take their place, and since the spring the Flood-Callers, who cut burial boats loose on the channels by the roads (quiet once their Caller at Oulnauve is down). What walks the roads is the reedfolk's own life: eel-carriers between the Landing and Moreva, lantern-sellers on the Westway, the Guild's tithe-cart and its bailiffs, burial processions singing to the water, the lamplighter at dusk.

name: The Flood-Callers at the channel
notes: Flood-Callers cutting a burial boat loose where a road runs by a channel. The woman on the boards is one of them. Stops once the Caller at the Stakes at Oulnauve is down (core:quest/lanterns_taken_up).

talk.say: They cut my mother's lantern loose — there, on the water, it's going out—

lines.speaker: An Ebb-Hand
lines.spring: Let it go out! They are coming home!

name: A log by the bridge
notes: A sallowjaw lying as a log in the ditch where the road crosses water.

name: Lanterns off the road
notes: Two lights at the right height, the right amber, off the causeway over water deeper than it looks.

name: A burial going to the water

talk.prompt: Sing the third voice with them
talk.say: — You know the round? Then the third, under us, and slow. — There. She'll go out further for that. The water heard a stranger sing for her, and it listens for strangers.

hook.rumour: The mourners say the lanterns burn longest from {place}.

talk.prompt: Walk a verse with the lamplighter
talk.say: A verse a pole; that's how long a wick takes to catch. — You're walking the boards after dark? Then walk them after me, and keep to the lit side. The drowned climb the dark poles.

hook.rumour: The lamplighter says there is a light nobody lit at {place}.

talk.say: On three — no, on the round's third line, that's when you push — there! She floats. Take an eel liver for your trouble; it's good for the blood, whatever the Isseva bleeders say.
Guild business. If you've seen a man with a sack of eels and no tally-chalk on it, you've seen a thief. If you haven't, you haven't. Good day.

hook.rumour: The bailiff says the Guild counts its eels at {place}.

consequence.notice: You struck a Guild bailiff. The Tallymen write everything down.
consequence.killing_notice: A Guild bailiff is dead on a marsh road, and there is a column in Lantern Row for that.

talk.say: They're the Guild's, those two, and the eels were the marsh's before they were anybody's. — Here. And there's a dry place in the reeds where they never look.

talk.prompt: Point the bailiffs after the poacher
talk.say: That way? Obliged. The Guild remembers who helps it count.

consequence.killing_notice: A Guild bailiff is dead on a marsh road.

name: Eel-carriers
notes: Moreva's catch walked to the Landing in wet baskets on a packhorse, a carrier at its head and a boardwalker beside.

talk.say: Live eels, smoked eels, eel-skin for your boots. The live ones are the Landing's, mind; the smoked ones I can sell you.
The hounds come up the channel after the baskets at night. We walk in the day. So should you.

consequence.notice: The Reed Council will hear you set on the eel-carriers.
consequence.killing_notice: An eel-carrier lies dead on the channel track, and the marsh keeps its own count.

rescue.say: The baskets are all still wet. That's the whole of what I care about. Take a smoked one; take two.

name: Lantern-sellers from Isseva
notes: Isseva's lantern-makers carrying frames and indigo paper up the Westway to Nauvissa and back.

talk.say: Burial lanterns are made to measure, so I don't carry those. Everything else that burns, I do.
Mind the frames. Every one's pegged by hand and they don't like being knocked.

consequence.notice: The Reed Council will hear you set on the lantern-sellers.
consequence.killing_notice: A lantern-seller is dead on the Westway, and somebody will have to make her lantern.

rescue.say: Not one frame cracked. — Here. And a lantern, for the road; it's not a burial one, it's for you.

name: The Guild's tithe-cart
notes: The Tallymen's tenth of the Delta's eels going between Isseva and Oulea on a cart, a Guild carter and two bailiffs. Its load is the Guild's while the carter lives.

talk.say: The tithe's not for sale. What's on the tailboard is. Guild prices; I don't make them.
One in ten, by the Charter. Stand off the wheels.

consequence.notice: You set on the Guild's tithe-cart. Lantern Row will hear of it.
consequence.killing_notice: A Guild man is dead beside the tithe-cart, and the Tallymen keep count.

rescue.say: The tithe's all here. The Guild will write down that you helped; it writes down everything.

name: The bride-weavers' withies
notes: The Bride-Weavers carrying withies out to the Flood-Bride's frame; carry a bundle and they say where she stands.

talk.prompt: Carry a bundle of withies for the weavers
talk.say: Bless you. Up on your shoulder — that's it. They're for next spring's bride; this spring's turned on us, and Orrin says the next must be bound tighter. — You'll see her from the causeway. Don't stand between her and the water after dark.

hook.rumour: The weavers say the Bride who turned stands at {place}.

name: A wisp got loose
notes: The wisp-catcher's boy has dropped a jar on the causeway and the wisp is circling him; put it out and he'll take you to his master's rack in his talk.

talk.say: I dropped it — I only — it was Ferrit's best, number nine, and the glass went and it came out and it won't go away, it keeps looking at me. — If you put it out the glim's worth a lot. Don't tell Ferrit. Tell Ferrit. He's on the North Channel by the Eelfathom, under the jars.

hook.rumour: The boy's master hangs his jars at {place}.

name: Stakes in the fen
notes: A Guild surveyor staking out the next drain and a reedfolk stake-puller pulling the stakes up behind him; help one or the other.

talk.prompt: Hold the chain for the Guild surveyor
talk.say: Obliged. Forty links — mark — forty links — mark. The Guild's draining this side next, now the Dredge has found what it found. Not that the Dredge's crew will see it. — Here. Guild rates.

hook.rumour: The surveyor says the Guild's dredge is digging at {place}.

talk.prompt: Help the reedfolk pull the Guild's stakes
talk.say: That's it, rock it, it comes. — Every one he puts in I take out; he'll be at it till he's old. They're draining toward the Builders' street the Dredge dug into, west of Isseva. Nobody's come up out of that hole in three weeks. The marsh takes back what's dug.

hook.rumour: The stake-puller says nobody has come up out of {place}.

name: A drowned man asking the way
notes: At night a drowned man sits by the causeway asking the way to Saeva, where he lived; walk him there and he goes into the water, and says where his crew musters.

talk.prompt: Ask the wet man what he wants
talk.say: — Which way is {place}? I lived there. I had a house. I came up the flats with the others and I can't find the road; the reeds are all wrong. Walk me there. I won't touch you. I'm cold.
talk.thanks: — There. The roofs. That one was mine. — Thank you. I'll go down to the water now; the others are waiting at the barrow with the ship's posts, out on the flats past the Saltgate. We're to go aboard at the spring tide. — Don't come.

hook.rumour: The drowned man said his crew musters at {place}.

name: A ropewalker measuring the causeway
notes: A Hask cousin walking the causeway with a knotted measuring-rope for the Council's new boardwalk.

talk.say: The causeway, for the Council; they want new boards and they want to know how many. Four hundred and six Hask paces from the last pole. — It's a Hask rope, this; knotted every pace. Corra walked my name into it so it wouldn't lie to me. She'll walk yours in too, if you go out to the ropewalk.

hook.rumour: The Hasks walk names into their rope at {place}.

name: A man with one boot
notes: A Guild bailiff off duty, one boot on, who will not say where the other went; he points you away from the Sundew Garden, which tells you where it is.

folk.name: A man in one Guild boot

talk.say: What boot. — There is one boot. I am wearing it. — If you are going east past the Landing, do not go into the herb-wife's garden, and if you do go into it, do not stand by the tub, and if you do stand by the tub, do not, whatever she says, take your boots off to wade. — I am not missing. Tell the Guild I am not missing.

hook.rumour: The one-booted man said not to go near the tub at {place}.
